function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  For the most up‑to‑date figure you can check one of the following reliable sources:

| Source | Typical URL |
|--------|-------------|
| **Bloomberg** | https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/commodities |
| **Kitco** | https://www.kitco.com/ |
| **Reuters** | https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities |
| **London Bullion Market Association (LBMA)** | https://www.lbma.org.uk/ |
| **U.S. Treasury / Federal Reserve** | https://www.federalreserve.gov/ |

These sites publish the current spot price of gold in U.S. dollars per troy ounce, usually updated several times per minute during trading hours. If you need a quick snapshot, you can also look at financial news apps (e.g., CNBC, Bloomberg Terminal) or commodity trackers on your phone.

So answer: I don't have real-time data. Suggest checking reliable sources like Bloomberg, Kitco, etc.
